transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-27
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Meyers (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Carlos Vega (Redwood Solutions Eng), Ethan Park (Lacuna Head of ML), Sofia Martinez (PM), Liam O'Connor (SRE), Nadia Li (Localization)

Summary:
Quick scoping call to align on scope for a POC focused on multilingual invoice extraction (10 languages, EU+NA), define success criteria (precision/recall targets by field), understand workload size (avg tokens per doc, concurrency), and plan a small benchmark run on open models via Redwood hosted and dedicated routing options. Discussed tradeoffs (latency vs cost, quantized weights vs FP16), data residency and audit logs for EU region.

Topics covered:
- POC goals and timeline
- Data set and language coverage
- Workload sizing and throughput expectations
- Model shortlist ideas and quality tradeoffs
- Benchmark plan and metrics (QA sets, latency p50/p95, cost per doc)
- Deployment modes (hosted vs dedicated vs private VPC)
- Security requirements (SSO, KMS, retention)

(00:00) Jordan Meyers: hey everyone, thanks for joining, can you hear me all right?
(00:04) Ethan Park: yes, loud and clear, thx Jordan.
(00:07) Priya Singh: good afternoon, im Priya from the SE team, i'll focus on perf and bench details.
(00:12) Sofia Martinez: hi, Sofia, PM on invoices, excited to scope this out.
(00:16) Liam O'Connor: Liam here, i look after infra and SRE concerns.
(00:20) Jordan Meyers: quick agenda — align success criteria, confirm dataset and languages, sizing, and agree next steps. maybe 45 minutes then we iterate. sound ok?
(00:28) Nadia Li: also want to highlight localization edge cases — cursive fonts, mixed-language fields in invoices.

(01:05) Ethan Park: to ground the convo, our main requirement: field extraction for invoice number, vendor name, total_amount, tax_breakdown. We're also evaluating vendor matching confidence score. Target is high precision on totals (>=98%) and recall on line items >=92% but we can be pragmatic.
(01:30) Priya Singh: got it. for the POC scope it's helpful to pick 2 tiers of truth: strict for totals/tax and relaxed for vendor-name matching, since names vary. For measurement we'll use token-level and entity-level F1.

(02:10) Jordan Meyers: workload sizing — Ethan, what's your volume? concurrency? expected peak?
(02:16) Ethan Park: right now in prod we process ~180k invoices/month, peak batch days up to 12k/day. For the POC initial slice we'd like to run 5k docs over 2 weeks, but also simulate spike concurrency of ~30 qps for extraction microservice.
(02:35) Carlos Vega: 30 qps for NLP extraction ok, that's modest. need to know average seq length after OCR — tokens per invoice?
(02:42) Liam O'Connor: our OCR pipeline yields roughly 1.2k tokens per invoice on average, but some large invoices hit 6k tokens. we can sample and give distribution.
(02:50) Priya Singh: good, that distribution matters for batching and KV cache sizing. we normally test p50/p95 seq lengths to choose batch windows and kernel selection.

(03:30) Sofia Martinez: languages -- we need English, Spanish, French, German, Dutch, Polish, Portuguese, Italian, Swedish, and occasional Japanese. Localization team will provide language breakdown.
(03:45) Nadia Li: note Japanese has different tokenization and OCR noise, will need special prompts and possibly model with better CJK handling.

(04:20) Jordan Meyers: model shortlist — initial thinking from Redwood: a mix of 1) a strong 70B open encoder-decoder quantized model tuned for extraction, 2) a compact 13B variant with instruction tuning, 3) a multilingual 30B that historically handles EU languages well, and 4) a baseline small 7B for throughput comparison. we can provide names and performance profiles in the follow-up.
(04:45) Ethan Park: any thoughts on accuracy differences between the 30B and 70B for vendor matching? costs will matter.
(04:53) Priya Singh: empirically the 70B gives better zero-shot layout/occr robustness — usually 3-7% absolute on F1 for messy docs vs 30B. but latency and unit cost go up severalx. with Redwood Optimize we can show batching/quant tradeoffs that reduce cost while preserving most quality.

(05:30) Liam O'Connor: on infra mode: we prefer hosted for speed, but EU data residency + audit logs are required for regulated clients. is Redwood Private an option?
(05:40) Jordan Meyers: yes, Private (VPC) is available; we can run the control plane in Redwood but data and inference in an EU region or on a dedicated pool. we support KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs. for the POC we can demo hosted EU region and if it meets needs, propose a dedicated pool for production.

(06:20) Sofia Martinez: how fast can we get benchmarks? we want a quick run to decide on model choice within two weeks.
(06:28) Priya Singh: we can run an initial sweep within 3-4 days after you send sample data. that would be lightweight (10-20% of docs) to get initial p50/p95 latencies and token costs. full run across all languages maybe 7-10 business days.

(07:05) Ethan Park: success criteria — let's be explicit: accuracy: total_amount precision >=98%, total_amount recall >=95%, invoice_number F1 >=96%, vendor name recall >=90% (with human review for borderline cases). Latency: per-doc extraction p95 < 750ms in production for single-invoice requests, or for batch processing throughput of 30 qps sustained. Cost: target cost per invoice < $0.02 (we know this is tight).
(07:40) Priya Singh: that cost target depends heavily on model choice and batching — with a quantized 13B we can be closer to that cost but might underperform on messy docs. we should include a human-in-loop fallback for vendor-name verification to keep cost bounded.

(08:20) Carlos Vega: regarding benchmarking metrics, we'll capture: field-level precision/recall, end-to-end extraction latency (cold/warm), tokens/kg (cost proxy), and percent of docs flagged for human review. We'll also run stress tests for concurrency to validate autoscaling.

(09:05) Liam O'Connor: SSO and RBAC — we'll need SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning for users, and role-based access for the audit logs. encryption at rest with customer KMS is mandatory. can Redwood support HSM-backed KMS?
(09:20) Jordan Meyers: yes — Redwood Private supports customer KMS and HSM integration. hosted can also integrate with cloud KMS in EU region. we'll include security docs.

(10:00) Sofia Martinez: one risk is OCR noise; do you recommend cleaning at OCR stage or rely on model prompts to normalize?
(10:08) Priya Singh: both. best results come from a light OCR normalization (remove headers, unify date formats) plus robust prompt engineering. for multilingual cases, custom tokenization and language-specific prompts help. we often run small prompt sweeps as part of the bench.

(11:00) Ethan Park: any required artifacts from Redwood for procurement? SOC2 type II, data processing agreement, and EU data residency attestation.
(11:10) Jordan Meyers: we'll attach our compliance pack (SOC2, ISO summary), sample DPA, and private deployment whitepaper in the follow-up.

(12:00) Priya Singh: back to model tradeoffs: we propose these concrete candidates — not model vendor names but size/trait descriptors:
- Model A: 70B multilingual, high-quality, FP16 or int8 quantizable, best for messy OCR
- Model B: 30B multilingual balanced, strong EU languages, lower latency than A
- Model C: 13B quantized cost-optimized, decent for clean OCR and high throughput
- Model D: 7B baseline for throughput baseline and fallback routing

(12:40) Sofia Martinez: ok — to prioritize, we want to see empirical F1 on our sample set and the cost/latency matrix. also include a recommendation for which model to use in canary vs production.

(13:10) Jordan Meyers: for the POC plan timeline i suggest:
- By 2026-03-31: Lacuna shares samples + language breakdown
- 2026-04-01: Redwood delivers model shortlist + bench plan + cost estimates
- 2026-04-06 to 2026-04-10: lightweight bench sweep (10-20% samples)
- 2026-04-13 to 2026-04-20: full benchmark and SLA tuning, iterate on prompts
- 2026-04-27: POC review + recommended production plan

(14:10) Ethan Park: that timeline works for us as long as cost estimates are clear.

(14:40) Carlos Vega: small note on metrics collection — we'll provide a benchmark sheet template (CSV) you can fill with ground truth; we'll compute per-field metrics and visualize.

(15:05) Nadia Li: one nuance: Japanese invoices sometimes embed English amounts in different formats; expect increased false negatives. can we have a plan to isolate CJK in the bench?
(15:15) Priya Singh: yes we'll tag language-specific subset and run CJK-specific runs with tailored prompts and tokenizers.

(16:00) Sofia Martinez: procurement wise, what does a short-term POC contract look like if we need dedicated pool for benchmarking?
(16:08) Jordan Meyers: we can do a short POC engagement (30 days) with a reserved pool + bench credits. cost depends on chosen capacity; we'll include options in the follow-up.

(16:45) Ethan Park: are there recommended fallback policies if model latency spikes?
(16:50) Priya Singh: yes — Redwood supports smart routing: fallback to smaller model for non-critical fields, or route to canary region. we can demo automatic degrade policies in the POC.

(17:20) Jordan Meyers: ok let's capture next steps again — i'll send the model shortlist + cost spreadsheet. Priya will run bench harness and propose SLO/cost tradeoff matrix. Ethan/Sofia will send samples and confirm acceptance criteria.

(17:45) Sofia Martinez: thanks everyone, this was helpful. we'll sync on the samples today.
(17:50) Jordan Meyers: great, thanks all, talk soon.

Recap / Action items (repeat):
- Redwood: model shortlist + bench plan + compliance pack (SOC2, DPA, EU residency note) by 2026-04-01.
- Customer: Provide anonymized invoice samples (PDF + OCR text) and language distribution by 2026-03-31.
- Redwood SE: prepare benchmark harness and latency/cost SLO matrix by 2026-04-03.

References mentioned: "benchmark sheet" (will be shared as CSV), POC engagement template, Redwood Private whitepaper, compliance pack.

End of transcript.
